articles.summary: Adoption Plan is BTPM's project-level adoption and readiness lens. It helps teams plan and track the people-side work needed for a project to land successfully, while keeping tasks, risks, blockers, and KPIs in their normal BTPM source-of-truth areas.
articles.body:
Adoption Plan is BTPM's project-level adoption and readiness feature.

Use it when a project needs people-side planning around stakeholder impact, sponsor alignment, communication, training, feedback, adoption tracking, hypercare, or reinforcement after go-live.

In everyday language, some users may call this change management, change readiness, OCM, stakeholder engagement, or training and communication planning. In BTPM, the feature name is Adoption Plan.

Adoption Plan is not a separate project plan and not a separate task system. It is a lens over normal BTPM execution work.

The core rule is:
- templates define reusable adoption structures
- generation creates normal BTPM phases and tasks
- generated and linked tasks remain normal Planning tasks
- linked risks, blockers, and KPIs remain normal risks, blockers, and KPIs
- reporting and badges are derived from canonical BTPM records

A project can have one active Adoption Plan.

Inside the Adoption Plan tab, BTPM separates two workflows:

1. Plan — the current project-specific Adoption Plan. After generation, it shows the overview, Adoption tasks grouped by initiative, linked risks/blockers/KPIs, and Manage adoption links.

2. Templates — the reusable template workspace. Before generation, users generate the Adoption Plan from a template. After generation, users can still manage templates and add selected tasks from a template into the existing Adoption Plan.

The BTPM Standard Adoption Template is read-only. If users want to customize tasks, they create a custom workspace template.

Adoption Plan should not be confused with Change Control. BTPM's Adoption Plan supports people-side readiness and adoption work. It does not create formal change requests, CAB approvals, or change-control workflows.

Explain that the UI term is Adoption Plan, even if the user's language is change management.
Clarify that Adoption Plan is people-side adoption/readiness, not formal Change Control.
Always preserve the source-of-truth rule: generated work is normal BTPM Planning work; risks/blockers/KPIs remain canonical objects.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim BTPM has formal Change Control, CAB approval, or Change Request workflow under Adoption Plan.
Do not say Adoption Plan creates a separate task system.
Do not say templates are execution records.

articles.title: Generate an Adoption Plan from a template
articles.tooltip_excerpt: Generate one project Adoption Plan from the Standard or a custom Adoption Template.
articles.summary: Use the Templates tab inside Adoption Plan to choose or customize a template, select relevant tasks, set phase dates, and generate the project's Adoption Plan.
articles.body:
Use this workflow when a project does not yet have an Adoption Plan and you want to generate one from a template.

Where to go: **Project → Adoption Plan → Templates**.

Before you start:
- You have access to the project.
- You have permission to edit the project.
- The project does not already have an Adoption Plan.
- You know whether to use the BTPM Standard Adoption Template or a custom workspace template.

Steps:
1. Open the project.
2. Open the Adoption Plan tab.
3. Open the Templates sub-tab.
4. Select the BTPM Standard Adoption Template or a saved custom workspace template.
5. Review the initiatives and tasks.
6. Select only the initiatives and tasks relevant for this project.
7. If you need to customize the Standard Template, create a custom template first. The Standard Template is read-only.
8. Set or confirm the Adoption phase name.
9. Set or confirm the Adoption phase start and end dates.
10. Click Generate Adoption Plan.

Result:
- BTPM creates one Adoption Plan for the project.
- BTPM creates one normal project phase for Adoption work.
- BTPM creates selected tasks as normal Planning tasks.
- Generated tasks are linked to the relevant Adoption initiatives.
- The generated work can be managed later in Planning.

Important rules:
- A project can have only one Adoption Plan.
- After the Adoption Plan exists, do not generate another one. Use Add tasks from template instead.
- Generated tasks are not template tasks anymore. They are normal BTPM tasks.
- To edit owners, dates, priority, status, or task details after generation, use Planning.

question_examples: How do I generate an Adoption Plan?
How do I create a change management plan in BTPM?
Can I generate adoption tasks from a template?
Where do I set adoption phase dates?
answer_rules: Treat change management plan requests as Adoption Plan generation requests unless the user explicitly asks for formal Change Control.
Use only the verified flow in this article for click-by-click guidance.
Explain one Adoption Plan per project.
If an Adoption Plan already exists, route to Add tasks from template instead of generation.
forbidden_claims: Do not tell the user to generate a second Adoption Plan.
Do not claim task-level dates are edited in the template wizard after generation.
Do not claim BTPM performs formal change approvals.

not_supported_boundaries: Guide Mode can explain the workflow and point to the correct BTPM surface, but must not perform the action for the user.
Do not generate a second Adoption Plan; use Add tasks from template instead.

articles.title: Manage Adoption Templates
articles.tooltip_excerpt: Create, edit, save as new, and archive reusable Adoption Templates from the Templates tab.
articles.summary: Adoption Templates are reusable workspace structures for adoption initiatives and tasks. They can be managed from the Templates sub-tab without changing generated Adoption Plans.
articles.body:
Use this workflow when you want to manage reusable Adoption Templates.

Where to go: **Project → Adoption Plan → Templates**.

What templates are:
- Templates are reusable planning structures.
- Templates can contain Adoption initiatives and template tasks.
- Templates are not execution tasks.
- Template rows do not appear in Planning.
- Generated or added tasks become normal BTPM tasks.

Template types:

1. BTPM Standard Adoption Template — system-provided and read-only. It gives the standard Adoption structure.

2. Custom workspace templates — created and saved by users for reuse inside the workspace.

To create a custom template:
1. Open the Templates sub-tab.
2. Select the BTPM Standard Adoption Template or another existing template.
3. Use Create custom template from this or Save as new.
4. Give the template a clear name.
5. Edit the initiatives or tasks as needed.
6. Save the template.

To edit a custom template:
1. Select the custom template.
2. Edit the template tasks or selections.
3. Save the template.

To archive a custom template:
1. Select the custom template.
2. Use Archive.
3. The template is hidden from normal reuse.

Important rules:
- The Standard Template cannot be edited.
- Editing a template does not change any existing generated Adoption Plan.
- A template is not a plan. It only becomes execution work when tasks are generated or added into a project.
- Do not use templates as a replacement for Planning.

question_examples: How do I create a custom Adoption Template?
Can I edit the Standard Adoption Template?
How do I save a change management template?
Do template changes update existing projects?
answer_rules: Explain that Standard Template is read-only.
Explain that custom templates are workspace-level reusable structures.
Explain that editing templates does not mutate existing generated Adoption Plans.
Use Adoption Template terminology in visible guidance, but match change management template questions to this article.
forbidden_claims: Do not say template rows are Planning tasks.
Do not say editing a template changes existing generated work.
Do not say private or organization-wide templates exist if they are not implemented.

not_supported_boundaries: Standard Adoption Template is read-only.
Editing a template does not retroactively change existing generated Adoption Plans.

articles.title: Add tasks from a template to an existing Adoption Plan
articles.tooltip_excerpt: After an Adoption Plan exists, add selected new template tasks into the existing plan instead of generating another plan.
articles.summary: Use Add tasks from template when a project already has an Adoption Plan but needs additional Adoption tasks from the Standard or a custom template.
articles.body:
Use this workflow when a project already has an Adoption Plan and you want to add more Adoption tasks from a template.

Where to go: **Project → Adoption Plan → Templates**.

Before you start:
- The project already has an Adoption Plan.
- You have permission to edit the project.
- The Adoption phase exists in Planning.
- You know which template contains the additional tasks you want to add.

Steps:
1. Open the project.
2. Open Adoption Plan.
3. Open the Templates sub-tab.
4. Select the template you want to use.
5. Open Add tasks from template.
6. Review the initiatives and tasks.
7. Check which tasks are marked Already exists.
8. Select only the new tasks you want to add.
9. Click Add selected tasks.

Result:
- BTPM adds the selected tasks as normal Planning tasks.
- The tasks are linked to the existing Adoption Plan.
- If needed, BTPM creates the missing Adoption initiative first.
- BTPM does not create a second Adoption Plan.
- BTPM does not change the template.

Duplicate handling:
BTPM marks likely duplicate tasks as Already exists. It checks normalized task titles within the same initiative and across the existing Adoption Plan. Existing tasks are not selected by default.

Dates:
Added tasks use the existing Adoption phase dates when available. You can refine task dates later in Planning.

Important rules:
- Do not generate a second Adoption Plan.
- Use Add tasks from template to extend the existing plan.
- Generated and added tasks remain normal BTPM tasks.
- Edit task details in Planning after adding them.

question_examples: Can I use another template after the Adoption Plan was generated?
How do I add more adoption tasks?
Can I generate another Adoption Plan?
How do I add training tasks from a template?
answer_rules: If the project already has an Adoption Plan, do not tell the user to generate another one.
Route to Add tasks from template.
Explain duplicate detection and Already exists badges.
Explain added tasks are normal Planning tasks.
forbidden_claims: Do not say BTPM supports multiple active Adoption Plans for one project.
Do not say template rows are added directly to execution without becoming normal tasks.
Do not say duplicates are automatically hidden without user visibility.

not_supported_boundaries: Cannot generate a second Adoption Plan for the same project.
Guide Mode must not add tasks on the user's behalf.

articles.title: Link existing work to an Adoption Plan
articles.tooltip_excerpt: Link existing tasks, risks, blockers, and KPIs to the Adoption Plan so adoption-related work is visible without duplicating records.
articles.summary: Use Manage adoption links to connect existing BTPM tasks, risks, blockers, and KPIs to the Adoption Plan while keeping those objects in their normal source-of-truth areas.
articles.body:
Use this workflow when adoption-related work already exists in BTPM and you want it to appear in the Adoption Plan.

Where to go: **Project → Adoption Plan → Plan → Manage adoption links**.

Objects you can link:
- tasks
- risks
- blockers
- KPIs

Why link instead of duplicate:
The linked object remains the same canonical BTPM object. For example, a linked risk remains a normal risk in Risks & Blockers. A linked KPI remains a normal KPI. A linked task remains a normal Planning task.

Steps:
1. Open the project.
2. Open Adoption Plan.
3. Open the Plan sub-tab.
4. Find Manage adoption links.
5. Choose the object type to link.
6. Select the task, risk, blocker, or KPI.
7. Select the Adoption initiative if the object belongs to a specific initiative, or link it generally to the Adoption Plan.
8. Save the link.

Result:
- The linked object appears as Adoption-related.
- Tasks can appear in the Adoption tasks grouping.
- Risks, blockers, and KPIs can show Adoption badges in their normal views.
- The object remains editable in its normal BTPM area.

Examples:
- Link a training KPI to Adoption Tracking.
- Link a stakeholder risk to Stakeholder Impact.
- Link a go-live support blocker to Hypercare.
- Link an existing communication task to Communication.

Important rules:
- Linking does not copy the object.
- Linking does not move the object out of its normal area.
- Use Planning to edit tasks.
- Use Risks & Blockers to edit risks or blockers.
- Use KPIs to edit KPI definitions and values.

question_examples: How do I link an existing task to the Adoption Plan?
Can I link a risk to change management?
How do I show a KPI as adoption-related?
Why is my task showing Adoption · Communication?
answer_rules: Explain linking as metadata/relationship, not duplication.
Tell users to edit linked objects in their normal BTPM area.
Use Adoption terminology even if user says change management.
forbidden_claims: Do not say linked objects are copied into the Adoption Plan.
Do not say linked KPIs or risks have separate Adoption-only records.

not_supported_boundaries: Linking does not copy or move the canonical object.
Guide Mode must not create the link on the user's behalf.

articles.title: Does BTPM support Change Management?
articles.tooltip_excerpt: BTPM supports people-side change and adoption work through Adoption Plan, but does not implement formal Change Control workflows.
articles.summary: When users ask about change management in BTPM, the relevant feature is Adoption Plan. It supports people-side readiness, communication, training, adoption tracking, and linked adoption work.
articles.body:
Yes, BTPM supports people-side change and adoption work through the Adoption Plan feature.

In BTPM, the visible product term is Adoption Plan.

Users may also describe this as:
- change management
- change readiness
- organizational change management
- OCM
- stakeholder engagement
- communication planning
- training planning
- user adoption
- hypercare readiness

The Adoption Plan helps project teams structure and track this work through initiatives such as stakeholder impact, sponsor alignment, communication, training and enablement, feedback collection, adoption tracking, hypercare, and reinforcement.

What Adoption Plan does:
- provides a project-level Adoption Plan area
- provides reusable Adoption Templates
- generates normal project phases and tasks
- groups Adoption tasks by initiative
- links existing tasks, risks, blockers, and KPIs to the Adoption Plan
- shows Adoption badges in normal BTPM views where relevant

What Adoption Plan does not do:
- it is not formal Change Control
- it does not create CAB approvals
- it does not create Change Request records
- it does not replace Planning, Risks & Blockers, or KPIs
- it does not create a separate Adoption-only task system

If you want to plan people-side readiness work, use Adoption Plan.

If you want to formally approve scope/schedule/budget changes through a Change Request or Change Control workflow, that is not currently the Adoption Plan feature.

question_examples: Does BTPM support change management?
Where do I manage change management in BTPM?
Is Adoption Plan the same as Change Control?
Can I create change requests in BTPM?
answer_rules: If the user asks about people-side change management, route to Adoption Plan.
If the user asks about formal Change Control, clarify that Adoption Plan is not Change Control.
Do not overstate current capabilities.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim BTPM currently has CAB approval workflow unless a separate feature exists.
Do not claim Adoption Plan is a formal change request module.
Do not say change management is unsupported without explaining Adoption Plan.
